name: cloud-keyboard

modules._doc: Keyboard libs are shared from ../aa_cloud-superapp/libs/ via relative project references in settings.gradle.

libs:core._doc: Pulled in for the debug surface. core api-exposes libs:devtools and is what DECLARES the CONSTELLATION_DATA permission the fleet token provider is gated on; without it the keyboard is the one constellation app that serves no 380xx debug API, so a toolbar fault can only be guessed at from source.

libs:devtools._doc: The debug server itself - AppDebugServer binds its own port from libs/devtools/debug-ports.json (#792) and DebugInitProvider starts it. Listed because libs:core references it by project path.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:ui-kit._doc: 2026-10-16 owner decision: all apps must be Compose. Shared BY REFERENCE: the fleet's Compose kit (CloudKitTheme + KitImeComposeView) libs:media, libs:voice and libs:translate build their keyboard surfaces on; listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it.

libs:text-tools._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/ - settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy.
libs:text-tools._doc: The ITextTools binder. This APK SERVES it: libs:keyboard holds AiRouter (Enhance) and reaches libs:translate (Translate), so it is the only app that can answer, and the only one that ever sees the provider key. cloud-mail declares the same module to CALL it.

libs:autofill._doc: Tier 3 of the fleet autofill (a0_docs/eng-specs/autofill-3-tier.md): the Cloud Account non-secret SOT contract. libs:keyboard reads profiles and snippets through it (AUTOFILL_PROFILE_READ) for its row-2 candidates.

libs:ui-nav-bars._doc: #1352 Configs ▸ General and ▸ About (fleetconfigs): FleetConfigsActivity, started from this app's own menu. Shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:bottomnav._doc: libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency; listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:ui-icons._doc: libs:bottomnav's dependency; listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:theme-background._doc: libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency (the page background); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

keyboard_media._doc: Same block as aa_cloud-superapp — shared vault secret. build.sh sops-decrypts vault_secrets → TENOR_API_KEY/GIPHY_API_KEY env vars → Gradle BuildConfig → MediaRuntime.configure().

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps — the SAME key that signs the superapp, so the in-app fleet updater never hits INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR (default ~/git/cloud-vault) + sops-decrypts the passwords, and _enforce_signature re-signs the built APK with it. NO fallback: if the key is unavailable the build FAILS LOUD — it never signs with the ephemeral android debug keystore.

update._doc: #776 Config ▸ Update. This app compiles NO libs:updater and may not start to: #763's lib-classes ratchet (1_cicd/src/data/lib-classes.json, L4) counts every app that compiles a `logic` lib, and one more edge turns mesh-membership-guard red. Apps without an updater are checked, downloaded (with the #774 cached Download → Install → Clear stages), installed and auto-updated by the fleet Store, so the keyboard's Update page hands off to the Store's own row for it instead of hand-rolling a second updater. Baked into libs:keyboard's BuildConfig.UPDATE_B64 (libs/keyboard/build.gradle reads THIS file through rootDir); an empty store_package hides the page.
update._doc_store_extras: The SuperApp launcher's shortcut_action grammar (ShellActivity.handleShortcutIntent). page:config/store-cloud is Store ▸ Cloud Constellation, the same target the Store's own update notification uses (aa_cloud-superapp App.kt AppStoreHost.launchExtras) and declared in aa_cloud-superapp/build.json (page id store-cloud).
update._doc_fallback_url: Only when the SuperApp is not installed: the rolling GitHub release asset release.gh_release publishes.

analytics._doc: Consumed by :libs:analytics, which reads THIS file (rootDir) at build time and bakes the values into BuildConfig. Both backends are single-site today, so every app reports into the same site and is told apart by .app — give each app its own site_id once per-app sites exist in Umami/Matomo.

tests._doc: What CI runs to prove this app works. Read by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh. Until this block existed ship-cloud-keyboard.yml called the publish gate and assembleRelease and nothing else: it never invoked the test engine at all, so the green it reported meant only that the Kotlin compiled. The assertions that DO cover this keyboard were filed under aa_cloud-superapp/test/ and gate the superapp's release, not this one — a keyboard could ship broken with every one of them passing.

shell._doc_requires: Tools a tester shells out to, checked BEFORE anything runs. A missing tool does not fail a tester, it makes the tester answer from the tool's absence: four testers in this repository passed only because ripgrep was not installed and their invocation failed open. Neither tester here uses ripgrep, deliberately. python3 is the silence guard itself; awk extracts the Kotlin function bodies the structural assertions read, and an absent awk would hand them empty bodies to agree with.
shell._doc_quarantine: Filename to the REASON it may fail. Empty, and it should stay that way: a quarantined tester that starts PASSING fails the build, so an entry cannot outlive its reason. Anything not named here is fatal.

unit._doc: Left disabled HERE because this engine step runs before the JDK/SDK setup. The JVM tests that exist (libs:keyboard KeyboardViewStateTest, #843) run in their own ship-cloud-keyboard.yml step after the SDK setup, via ./build.sh unit (:libs:keyboard:testDebugUnitTest).

debug_api._doc: #776 the keyboard's own group on the fleet debug server (libs:devtools AppDebugServer, already compiled in through libs:core). /api/<group>/toolbar answers expected vs drawn toolbar icons and the last rebuild reason (helium314.keyboard.latin.suggestions.ToolbarStatus), so the empty-toolbar fault can be checked on the device instead of guessed at.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: A keyboard that translates and listens, on device
about.description: Cloud Keyboard is the fleet's input method: typing with on-device translation, voice input and bundled sticker packs. Translation and voice recognition run on the phone, so what you type does not leave the device; the AI Enhance tool, when you use it, goes through the fleet's own AI gateway. It exists because the keyboard sees every word typed on the phone and must therefore be the most trusted app of all.
features: No typing data leaves the phone
Enhance: rewrite a sentence through the fleet's AI
guide: Enable Cloud Keyboard in Android's keyboard settings and choose it.
Tap the globe to translate what you type.
Hold the microphone key to dictate.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. Usage analytics are opt-in and off by default; when allowed, events go only to the owner's self-hosted Umami and Matomo. It calls no fleet service: its data stays on the phone.

related.why: Longer text tools on the same AI routing.

about.credits: Built over libs:keyboard, derived from HeliBoard (github.com/Helium314/HeliBoard), GPL-3.0, by Helium314 and the AOSP keyboard authors; the APK is therefore GPL-3.0. The shell, translation, voice and stickers are the fleet's own code.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
